metadata.title: AI Decision Theory Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary references for 11 decision-theory primitives: expected utility, Bayesian decision, minimax regret, value of information, MCDA, risk aversion, real options, prospect theory, Ellsberg/Allais paradoxes, multi-armed bandit, and stochastic dominance

canonical_texts.name: Theory of Games and Economic Behavior
canonical_texts.description: von Neumann and Morgenstern (1944/1947). Foundational text for EU theory and the vNM utility theorem. Primary source for primitive #1 (expected utility).

canonical_texts.name: The Foundations of Statistics
canonical_texts.description: Savage (1954). Subjective expected utility, minimax regret rule, and the sure-thing principle. Primary source for primitives #1 (EU, subjective probability) and #3 (minimax regret).

canonical_texts.name: Applied Statistical Decision Theory
canonical_texts.description: Raiffa and Schlaifer (1961). Bayesian decision theory, EVPI, EVSI, and conjugate priors. Primary source for primitives #2 (Bayesian decision) and #4 (value of information).

canonical_texts.name: Information Value Theory
canonical_texts.description: Howard (1966). Formal definition of EVPI and EVSI for decision analysis. Primary source for primitive #4 (value of information).

canonical_texts.name: Risk Aversion in the Small and in the Large
canonical_texts.description: Pratt (1964). Arrow-Pratt measures of absolute and relative risk aversion, certainty equivalent. Primary source for primitive #6 (risk aversion).

canonical_texts.name: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
canonical_texts.description: Kahneman and Tversky (1979). Econometrica. Prospect theory value function, loss aversion, probability weighting. Primary source for primitive #8 (prospect theory).

canonical_texts.name: Advances in Prospect Theory: Cumulative Representation of Uncertainty
canonical_texts.description: Tversky and Kahneman (1992). Cumulative prospect theory. Extension to multiple outcomes. Secondary source for primitive #8.

canonical_texts.name: Risk, Ambiguity, and the Savage Axioms
canonical_texts.description: Ellsberg (1961). Quarterly Journal of Economics. Ambiguity aversion and violation of the sure-thing principle. Primary source for primitive #9 (Ellsberg paradox).

canonical_texts.name: Le comportement de l'homme rationnel devant le risque
canonical_texts.description: Allais (1953). Econometrica. Certainty effect and independence axiom violation. Primary source for primitive #9 (Allais paradox).

canonical_texts.name: Investment under Uncertainty
canonical_texts.description: Dixit and Pindyck (1994). Princeton University Press. Real options, option to defer/expand/abandon, irreversibility premium. Primary source for primitive #7 (real options).

canonical_texts.name: The Analytic Hierarchy Process
canonical_texts.description: Saaty (1980). AHP methodology, pairwise comparisons, consistency ratio. Primary source for primitive #5 (MCDA — AHP).

canonical_texts.name: Multiple Attribute Decision Making
canonical_texts.description: Hwang and Yoon (1981). TOPSIS and other MCDA methods. Primary source for primitive #5 (MCDA — TOPSIS).

canonical_texts.name: Some Aspects of the Sequential Design of Experiments
canonical_texts.description: Robbins (1952). Bulletin of the AMS. Foundational bandit problem formulation. Primary source for primitive #10 (multi-armed bandit).

canonical_texts.name: Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem
canonical_texts.description: Auer, Cesa-Bianchi, and Fischer (2002). Machine Learning. UCB1 algorithm, logarithmic regret bound. Primary source for primitive #10 (UCB policy).

canonical_texts.name: On the Likelihood that One Unknown Probability Exceeds Another
canonical_texts.description: Thompson (1933). Biometrika. Original Thompson sampling paper. Primary source for primitive #10 (Thompson sampling).

canonical_texts.name: A Tutorial on Thompson Sampling
canonical_texts.description: Russo et al. (2018). Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 11(1). Comprehensive Thompson sampling tutorial including Bayesian regret bounds. Primary source for primitive #10.

canonical_texts.name: Bandit Algorithms
canonical_texts.description: Lattimore and Szepesvári (2020). Cambridge University Press. Comprehensive bandit algorithms reference including UCB, Thompson sampling, and minimax regret. Primary source for primitive #10.

canonical_texts.name: Rules for Ordering Uncertain Prospects
canonical_texts.description: Hadar and Russell (1969). American Economic Review. First and second-order stochastic dominance definitions. Primary source for primitive #11 (stochastic dominance).

canonical_texts.name: Stochastic Dominance and Expected Utility: Survey and Analysis
canonical_texts.description: Levy (1992). Management Science 38(4). Survey of stochastic dominance theory and its relationship to expected utility. Primary source for primitive #11.

canonical_texts.name: Maxmin Expected Utility with Non-Unique Prior
canonical_texts.description: Gilboa and Schmeidler (1989). Journal of Mathematical Economics. Maxmin EU and Choquet expected utility under ambiguity. Secondary source for primitive #9 (Ellsberg).

canonical_texts.name: Statistical Decision Theory and Bayesian Analysis
canonical_texts.description: Berger (1985). Springer. Comprehensive Bayesian decision theory reference. Secondary source for primitive #2.

canonical_texts.name: Essays in the Theory of Risk Bearing
canonical_texts.description: Arrow (1971). Markham. Arrow-Pratt coefficient of absolute risk aversion and its applications. Secondary source for primitive #6.

canonical_texts.name: Microeconomic Theory
canonical_texts.description: Mas-Colell, Whinston, and Green (1995). Oxford University Press. Chapter 6: risk aversion, EU, CE. Secondary source for primitives #1 and #6.

canonical_texts.name: Real Options: Managerial Flexibility and Strategy in Resource Allocation
canonical_texts.description: Trigeorgis (1996). MIT Press. Real options taxonomy and valuation methods. Secondary source for primitive #7.

canonical_texts.name: Optimal Statistical Decisions
canonical_texts.description: DeGroot (1970). McGraw-Hill. Bayesian decision theory, sufficient statistics, sequential decision problems. Secondary source for primitive #2.

canonical_texts.name: Increasing Risk: I. A Definition
canonical_texts.description: Rothschild and Stiglitz (1970). Journal of Economic Theory 2(3). Mean-preserving spread and second-order stochastic dominance. Secondary source for primitive #11.

canonical_texts.name: Multiple Criteria Decision Analysis: An Integrated Approach
canonical_texts.description: Belton and Stewart (2002). Kluwer. Comprehensive MCDA reference covering WSM, AHP, TOPSIS, and outranking methods. Secondary source for primitive #5.

canonical_texts.name: Determinants of Corporate Borrowing
canonical_texts.description: Myers (1977). Journal of Financial Economics. Introduced the concept of real options as growth options in corporate finance. Secondary source for primitive #7.

canonical_texts.name: No-Regret is not enough! Bandits with General Constraints through Adaptive Regret Minimization
canonical_texts.description: Bernasconi, Castiglioni, Celli (ICML 2025, PMLR 267:3877-3898). Weakly adaptive primal-dual algorithms for bandits with general long-term constraints; best-of-both-worlds guarantees (sublinear regret + sublinear violations) for stochastic and adversarial inputs; first no-α-regret result for contextual bandits with linear constraints under adversarial contexts. UPDATE for primitive #10.

canonical_texts.name: Toward Efficient Exploration by Large Language Model Agents
canonical_texts.description: Arumugam, Griffiths (ICLR 2026). LLMs explicitly implement PSRL via three roles: posterior updater, sampler, and policy executor. Retains provably-efficient exploration guarantees; outperforms standard LLM agent designs on natural-language exploration tasks. UPDATE for primitive #10; cross-link to #4.

canonical_texts.name: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Regret Optimization
canonical_texts.description: Fiechtner, Blanchet (arXiv 2504.10796, April 2025). Bridges Wasserstein DRO with minimax regret (DRRO). Coincides with ERM up to first order under smoothness; NP-hard in general; convex relaxation proposed with strong empirical performance. UPDATE for primitive #3.

canonical_texts.name: Robust Decisions via Generative Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization
canonical_texts.description: NeurIPS 2025. Gen-WDRO: combines conditional normalizing flows with DRO; neural networks adaptively determine Wasserstein robustness radii; tractable convex reformulation under linear costs. Reduces conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO. UPDATE for primitive #3.

canonical_texts.name: Distributionally Robust Performative Optimization
canonical_texts.description: Jia, Wang, Dong, Hanasusanto (NeurIPS 2025 poster, arXiv:2407.01344). DRO framework for decision-dependent distributions (performative setting); repeated robust risk minimization algorithm; validated on strategic classification, revenue management, portfolio optimization. UPDATE for primitives #3 and #1.

canonical_texts.name: Online Decision-Focused Learning
canonical_texts.description: Capitaine et al. (ICLR 2026). Extends decision-focused learning to dynamic environments with shifting cost functions and data distributions. Two algorithms (DF-FTPL, DF-OGD) with first provable online static and dynamic regret bounds for predict-then-optimize pipelines. NEW extension context for primitive #4.

canonical_texts.name: A Dual Perspective on Decision-Focused Learning: Scalable Training via Dual-Guided Surrogates
canonical_texts.description: Rodriguez-Diaz, Bansak, Paulson (NeurIPS 2025). DGL method: refreshes dual variables periodically from the downstream solver and trains on dual-adjusted targets using simple surrogates between refreshes. Matches or exceeds state-of-the-art DFL with far fewer solver calls. Corroborates online DFL direction.

canonical_texts.name: Shaping the Next One Hundred Years: New Methods for Quantitative, Long-Term Policy Analysis
canonical_texts.description: Lempert, Popper, and Bankes (2003). RAND MR-1626. Foundational RDM / DMDU methodology: run candidate strategies over large ensembles of scenarios, identify scenarios of concern where strategies fail (via PRIM), iteratively redesign for robustness. Primary source for RDM pattern in patterns-scenarios-traps.md.

canonical_texts.name: Dynamic adaptive policy pathways: A method for crafting robust decisions for a deeply uncertain world
canonical_texts.description: Haasnoot et al. (2013). Global Environmental Change 23(2), 485–498. DAPP framework: maps sequences of policy choices (pathways) triggered by observable threshold-crossings (tipping points). Extends real options (#7) to multi-stage contingent planning under deep uncertainty. Primary source for DAPP extension in 07-real-options.md.

canonical_texts.name: DeLLMa: Decision Making Under Uncertainty with Large Language Models
canonical_texts.description: Liu, Fu, Yogatama, Neiswanger (ICLR 2025 Spotlight, arXiv:2402.02392). Multi-step inference-time framework: (1) forecast uncertain variables in-context, (2) elicit utility function, (3) identify EU-maximising action. Up to 40% accuracy improvement over direct prompting across 3 LLM families on structured decision tasks. Primary source for LLM-assisted VoI section in 04-value-of-information.md.

canonical_texts.name: Resource-rational analysis: Understanding human cognition as the optimal use of limited computational resources
canonical_texts.description: Lieder and Griffiths (2020). Behavioral and Brain Sciences. Normative framework for bounded rationality: agents are rational given their computational constraints. Provides grounding for resource-rational reframe of PT deviations in 08-prospect-theory.md.

canonical_texts.name: Exploring the bounded rationality in human decision anomalies through an assemblable computational framework
canonical_texts.description: Lu, Lu, Ren, Zhang (2025). Cognitive Psychology 156, 101713. PubMed 39813936. ARRM framework: modular computational account explaining PT anomalies (loss aversion, probability distortion) as cost-optimal resource allocation. Supports resource-rational reframe of Primitives #8 and #9.

canonical_texts.name: Online Multi-LLM Selection via Contextual Bandits under Unstructured Context Evolution
canonical_texts.description: arXiv:2506.17670 (2026). Online bandit policy for routing queries across multiple LLM backends; contextual embeddings as features; regret-bounded selection under distribution shift. Applied source for app-builder recipe (primitive #10, model routing).

canonical_texts.name: Decision-Centric Design for LLM Systems
canonical_texts.description: arXiv:2604.00414 (2026). Formalizes LLM orchestration decisions (model routing, adaptive inference scaling, adaptive retrieval) as explicit decision problems under utility theory; VoI methods for clarify-or-commit tradeoffs; applied decision-theory framework for production LLM systems. Applied source for app-builder recipe (primitive #4, VoI gating).

canonical_texts.name: Meta-Analysis of Empirical Estimates of Loss Aversion
canonical_texts.description: Brown, A. L., Imai, T., Vieider, F. M., and Camerer, C. F. (2024). Journal of Economic Literature 62(2), 485-516. Large-scale meta-analysis of 607 empirical loss-aversion estimates from 150 studies across economics, psychology, and neuroscience. Mean lambda = 1.955, 95% CI [1.820, 2.102] -- revises the widely cited Tversky-Kahneman (1992) point estimate of 2.25 downward after correcting for publication bias and methodological heterogeneity. UPDATE/CORRECTION for primitive #8.

canonical_texts.name: The ergodicity problem in economics
canonical_texts.description: Peters, O. (2019). Nature Physics 15, 1216-1221. Ergodicity economics: distinguishes the ensemble average (what expected utility computes) from the time average (the growth rate one actor experiences across repeated multiplicative bets). Foundational source for the non-ergodicity / ruin-risk expert-judgment addition to primitive #6 and SKILL.md.

canonical_texts.name: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
canonical_texts.description: Kelly, J. L. (1956). Bell System Technical Journal 35(4). Original Kelly criterion paper: growth-optimal bet sizing for repeated wagers with a known edge. Foundational source for the Kelly-criterion expert-judgment addition to primitive #6 and SKILL.md.
